quotes.text: Group and manage your readers by physical location.

old_evidence.text: Before you can use a reader, you must register it to a location.
After you create a location, you can’t change its country.
You can’t create or modify zones using the API.
Only the Connect account you authenticate as can access these locations.
For Bluetooth readers, the `location` of a ConnectionToken has no effect.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/locations-and-zones, the 2026-11-07 capture states the purpose of grouping/managing readers by physical location and offers Dashboard and API variants (new raw lines 5-14). It supplies no further prerequisites, actors or state transitions. The 2026-05-01 guide says the business must assign and register readers to Locations before taking payments, can group multiple readers per Location, and can optionally nest zones with at most one zone per Location. Dashboard operators create locations and zones, move locations and perform deletions after clearing relevant reader/location associations; an API integrator can create or update a Location but cannot create or modify zones. A Location country cannot change after creation, requiring a new Location and reader re-registration (old raw lines 8-36, old raw lines 40-105). Direct-charge Locations belong to the authenticated connected account accessed with Stripe-Account; destination-charge Locations belong to the platform and can optionally reference connected accounts using metadata. The backend can scope ConnectionTokens to smart readers assigned to a Location, leave the token unscoped by Location, or use Bluetooth readers for which location does not affect the token (old raw lines 124-126, old raw lines 150-152, old raw lines 174-180). source-stripe-terminal-locations-and-zones preserves these historical topics but needs conditional metadata, country qualifiers and deletion visibility.
